data.title: Asian Equities Rebound as Huang Reinstatement Sparks AI-Stock Rally
data.description:
By Ronnie Harui

Asian equities rebounded Tuesday morning after Jensen Huang's return as chief executive of Nvidia sparked a rally in artificial-intelligence stocks.

The U.S. chip maker's board on Monday reinstated Huang less than two weeks after pushing him out over issues including extramarital affairs. The decision followed intense pressure from Silicon Valley, Wall Street investors, and the White House.

"Huang reinstated as CEO triggers a tremendous tech-led 'risk-back-on' rally," said Vishnu Varathan, head of Macro Strategy for APAC at Mizuho Securities (Singapore). "Markets cheered the news of what is perceived to be stability returning to the wider AI sector as Nvidia with Jensen at the helm was deemed to be the requisite connective tissue of the industry."

However, the company and its reinstated leader face a series of investigations by entities ranging from the Securities and Exchange Commission to a committee of the board itself.

Asian equities rebounded from Monday's selloff. South Korea's Kospi climbed 7.1%, with chip-making index heavyweights SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics rising 8.8% and 6.5%, respectively. Kospi futures rose more than 6%, triggering a five-minute trading halt by Korea Exchange.

Japan's Nikkei Stock Average advanced 4.8%. Resonac Holdings, a supplier of front-end and back-end semiconductor packaging materials, surged 16.4%, Advantest, a manufacturer of automatic semiconductor test equipment for semiconductor industry, jumped 15.6%, and Murata Manufacturing, a manufacturer of electronic components, added 14.9%.

Malaysia's FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI advanced 1.3% and Singapore's FTSE Straits Times Index gained 1.3%.

"Jensen's return is particularly welcome for Asian technology stocks, many of which suffered collateral damage from Nvidia's leadership crisis," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Markets, in an email.

Meanwhile, crude oil futures were mixed as traders parsed ongoing tensions in the Middle East.

The U.S. is investigating Iran's potential involvement in dozens of cyberattacks against energy tankers amid worries that Tehran is widening the war with cyber operations and terror plots against Americans far from the Middle East.

As many as 50 ships carrying oil, liquefied petroleum, chemical products and other explosive substances are believed to have been attacked, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing U.S. officials and others familiar with the matter.

"Iran continues to attack vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, with [President] Trump announcing it has launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time of over the year," ANZ Research analysts said in a report. "Despite some improvement in inventories and product availability, the oil market remains under severe strain," the analysts added.

Front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures were little changed at $80.16 a barrel, while front-month Brent crude oil futures edged 0.1% lower to $89.28 a barrel, ICE data showed.

data.title: Asian stocks rally as Huang's Nvidia return revives AI trade
data.description:
Key points:
  • Asian shares tracking US higher as markets cheer on Huang's return
  • Taiex leads charge with more than 9% gain
  • Treasury yields, dollar climb as Fed rate hike bets grow

By Jiaxing Li

Asian shares leapt on Tuesday following a spectacular Wall Street surge as Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO sparked a relief rally in the battered AI trade, while Federal Reserve tightening bets lifted Treasury yields and the dollar.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) climbed 4.6%, bouncing back from an eight-month low and heading for its biggest single-day gain in two weeks.

Japan's Nikkei added 4.5% as traders returned from a local holiday. South Korea's KOSPI surged 7.5%, while Taiwanese shares TWSE:TAIEX jumped 9.1%.

Huang's comeback capped a whirlwind week of events that whipped markets and tore through the AI ecosystem, which has relied on Nvidia for everything from supplying chips to bankrolling the industry's massive buildout.

Shares of Nvidia surged 31.5% on Monday, marking their biggest daily percentage gain in 23 years and restoring nearly $1 trillion in value to the company.

Companies across the AI industry also rallied sharply, with the Nasdaq 100 , which is concentrated in megacap tech companies, jumping more than 6%.

"The return of the most important man in the AI industry to the helm of its most important company has eased fear and uncertainty about the AI trade, at least at the margins," despite lingering concerns about slowing AI investment and moderating earnings growth, said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.

There are other risks for the market as well, such as uncertainty over US interest rate policy, with investors set to focus on Wednesday's PCE Index data (USPCEY=ECI) ahead of the Fed's final meeting of 2026, he added.

S&P 500 futures were flat and Nasdaq futures edged down 0.2% early on Tuesday. The cash S&P 500 CBOE:SPX and Nasdaq Composite indexes surged 4.7% and 6.5%, respectively.

AI REBOUND LIFTS FED TIGHTENING BETS

The sharp AI rebound has also eased growth concerns and loosened financial conditions, reviving market bets for near-term Fed tightening and lifting front-end Treasury yields and the dollar.

Fed funds futures traders are now pricing in a hike at the Fed's December meeting as a certainty, compared with 89% odds on Friday, when stocks tumbled, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool. The market-implied chance of a supersized 50-basis-point increase in around 5%.

The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note rose for a second day and was last at 4.94%, and the yield on the 2-year note (US2YT=RR) rose to 4.69%. The dollar, meanwhile, hovered near a more than 19-month high against the euro.

In commodities, oil prices fell more than 3% to near a three-month low on rising supplies from the Middle East, which offset worries about shipping and refinery attacks in the region. Brent crude futures were flat at $89.50 a barrel after settling down 3.5% at $89.37 a barrel on Monday. (O/R)

Bullion recovered from a more than one-year low, with spot gold last up 0.7% at $3,657.97 per ounce as investors bought the dip. (GOL/)

data.title: Aroa Biosurgery Sees Myriad Sales Surge to Lift Half-Year Revenue by 24%
data.description:
Aroa Biosurgery has lifted first-half revenue 24% to A$45.9 million (NZ$55.7m), driven by rapid growth in its Myriad soft-tissue reconstruction products.

Myriad revenue rose 57% to A$25.4m (NZ$30.9m) in the six months to 30 September, accounting for 56% of total product sales.

The New Zealand medical device company increased its product gross margin to 88% from 85% as higher-margin direct sales became a larger share of its business.

Aroa expects full-year revenue in the lower half of its guidance range of A$94.7m–A$102.9m (NZ$115m–NZ$125m), with the normalised EBITDA forecast still between A$6.6m andA$9.1m (NZ$8m–NZ$11m), alongside A$6.6m (NZ$8m) of planned investment in growth.

The group ended September debt-free with cash and term deposits of A$23.6m (NZ$28.7m).

Direct Sales Drive Earnings

Direct sales contributed 68% of product revenue, up from 57% a year earlier, as Myriad growth more than offset softer sales to distribution partner TELA Bio.

Sales to TELA Bio declined 7% to A$14.7m (NZ$17.8m), with management anticipating a 20% full-year decline as the distributor works through commercial and inventory pressures.

Normalised EBITDA increased 145% to A$3.6m (NZ$4.3m), despite higher expenditure on the US sales operation, while operating cash inflow grew to A$4.9m (NZ$6m) from A$3.3m (NZ$4m).

Active customer accounts increased to 474 from 380, while the number of sales representatives meeting the company’s annualised productivity benchmark rose to 15 from nine.

Management is targeting more than 30% annual growth in direct revenue, including more than 35% growth in Myriad, while monitoring the weaker TELA Bio contribution, with the company strengthening its US commercial leadership and entering a co-promotion agreement with Mölnlycke Healthcare US for Endoform in post-acute settings.

Myriad Clinical Study

A prospective Myriad study covering 411 patients and 474 soft-tissue defects across 10 US centres reported a 0.7% deep-tissue infection rate and a median of one application per defect.

No infections or adverse events were definitively attributed to Myriad, strengthening the clinical evidence available for hospital and payer discussions.

A separate randomised controlled trial involving 143 patients found that 55% of diabetic foot ulcers treated with Symphony plus standard care closed within 12 weeks, compared with 35% under standard care alone.

Mean wound closure was 7.8 days faster for the Symphony group, although commercial uptake of that product remains at an early stage.

Chief executive officer Brian Ward expressed his pleasure with the result, adding that the company’s focus was “leveraging the growing clinical evidence to drive broader adoption, supported by our strengthened commercial leadership”.

data.title: Huang returns as Nvidia CEO after Trump intervention in abrupt board reversal
data.description:
Key points:
  • Trump says Huang's return poses no national security risk
  • Board launches probe into possible foreign intelligence efforts targeting Huang
  • Huang's comeback underscores Nvidia's deep dependence on influential co-founder
  • Nvidia shares close up 31.5%

By Deborah Mary Sophia, Anhata Rooprai and David Morgan

Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday under pressure from US President Donald Trump, a stunning reversal following his resignation over revelations of extramarital affairs, drawing approval from Wall Street and opposition from US lawmakers.

Huang's comeback caps a whirlwind week of events that roiled markets and tore through the AI ecosystem that has relied on Nvidia for everything from supplying chips to bankrolling the industry's massive buildout.

But the board's about-face — less than a week after Chair Harvey Jones said Nvidia would not rehire Huang as CEO because his personal behavior was inconsistent with the company's code of conduct — raises questions about its independence, governance experts said, even as the company's investigation remains unfinished.

Huang's comeback boosted Wall Street and sent Nvidia's shares soaring. The stock closed up 31.5%, adding nearly $1 trillion in market value, vaulting the chipmaker back to the position of the second-biggest company by market value after Apple . The gains were not enough, however, to erase all losses since Huang's resignation on November 12.

Nvidia said in a statement that based on US government input the board was confident that "Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk," a claim backed by Trump in an interview with CNBC.

Huang said in a statement that he was honored to return and "can’t wait to get back to work.” He returned to company headquarters to cheers from employees and said he was going to "be a better CEO the second time around," Business Insider reported, citing a person familiar with the matter.

"Jensen's return is not a total shock, but it does send a troubling message about the state of corporate governance in America," said James St. Aubin, chief investment officer at Ocean Park Asset Management. "Certain executives are going to be held to different standards if you are perceived to be a one of one," he said, adding Huang would still have to answer "some tough questions from Congress."

Lawmakers across party lines strongly objected to Huang's reinstatement and called on Congress to pass the Chip Security Act, a bill that seeks to stop legally exported advanced chips from being diverted to China, where their sales are restricted.

US Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said Trump was "putting his own financial interests ... before our national security," while Senator Pete Ricketts, a Nebraska Republican, said Huang's return "doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips."

TRUMP'S SUPPORT FOR HUANG

Huang returned at the strong urging of Trump, industry leaders including Elon Musk, and some investors. His departure had reverberated from Silicon Valley to Taipei. A petition calling for his reinstatement drew more than 180,000 signatures, underscoring the unusually strong support for an executive who stepped down amid controversy.

"I believe my intervention was very important to get Jensen Huang back," Trump told CNBC.

Trump owns between $11 million and $55 million in Nvidia stock, according to a Reuters review of his annual financial disclosure for 2025 and share trading disclosures for 2026. Monday’s surge in Nvidia shares could have boosted Trump's net worth by as much as $17 million. A White House spokesperson said Trump’s stock and bond portfolio was independently managed by third-party financial institutions and neither the president nor any member of his family had any ability to direct or influence how the portfolio was invested.

Nvidia's board did not mention Huang's affairs. Apart from Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman who is accused of having ties with Beijing, Huang is accused of having had intimate relationships with at least two Nvidia employees.

Jensen Huang has acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and apologized, but has not publicly addressed the individual alleged relationships in detail. China has denied the espionage allegations. Attempts by Reuters to reach Alice Huang have been unsuccessful.

"There were definitely a lot of people who wanted him back. The extent that the administration intervened, the extent that shareholders intervened, it will be impossible to know," said Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers. "But it tells us to some extent that Jensen Huang was too big to be fired."

CHINA IS KEY TO NVIDIA

The moves come as Nvidia faces heightened scrutiny in Washington over the flow of advanced AI chips to China. US authorities have tightened licensing rules for some chip shipments and overseas data centers serving Chinese companies, while lawmakers are preparing to question Huang, who has pushed for greater access to the Chinese market.

Huang has agreed to testify before the US Senate in a public hearing on December 3, the Senate Banking Committee said. Huang's personal spokesperson declined to comment.

Trump told CNBC that he had urged Nvidia to continue reviewing its compliance with US export controls to ensure it was adequately protecting national security. Trump, who visited Shenzhen last week, told CNBC he had spoken to Chinese President Xi Jinping about Huang.

Huang's exit from Nvidia threatened its business in China, Reuters reported on Monday, with some customers there cancelling or hesitating to place orders, jeopardizing billions in revenue.

The US on Monday was set to add Singapore-based chip firm Megaspeed, which is closely tied to an espionage investigation involving Nvidia, to its trade blacklist, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters.

The Nvidia board has formed a committee to investigate whether foreign intelligence efforts targeted Huang and another committee focused on national security and export controls.

The company is also facing multiple investigations over issues ranging from potential accounting irregularities to suspected chip smuggling, and a shareholder lawsuit accusing the company and Huang of defrauding shareholders by concealing Huang's relationship with Alice Huang.

data.title: Stock market holiday today: BSE, NSE to remain closed for Guru Nanak Jayanti
data.description:
Indian stock markets will remain closed today, November 24, on account of Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev (Guru Nanak Jayanti), with trading suspended across major segments on both the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Trading in equities, equity derivatives, securities lending and borrowing (SLBs), currency derivatives, and interest rate derivatives will remain shut for the day on both exchanges.

Meanwhile, the commodity derivatives segment will remain closed during the morning session from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm, but trading will resume in the evening session between 5:00 pm and 11:30 pm/11:55 pm.

Market activity on the NSE and BSE will resume on November 25 (Wednesday).

Indian equity benchmarks snapped their two-day winning streak and ended lower on November 23, with the Nifty falling 1.7 percent, marking its biggest single-day decline in nearly five months. Broad-based selling in auto, metal and financial stocks dragged the benchmarks lower.

At close, the Sensex was down 1,483.72 points or 1.77 percent at 82,435.99, and the Nifty was down 450.95 points or 1.75 percent at 25,349.65.

Biggest Nifty losers were Tata Steel, Axis Bank, ICICI Bank, Hindalco, HDFC Bank, while gainers included TCS, Tech Mahindra, Shriram Finance, HCL Technologies, Titan Company.

On the sectoral front, except Information Technology and Consumer Durables, all other sectoral indices ended in the red Metal, Oil & Gas, PSU Bank, Private Bank, Infra, Energy, Auto down 1-3 percent.

The broader markets outperformed the benchmark indices, with the Nifty Midcap index falling 0.7 percent, while the Nifty Smallcap index losing 0.66%.

"Markets witnessed sharp profit-booking on Monday, declining over 1.5%, following the recent four-week rally. After an initial uptick, the benchmark indices gradually drifted lower as the session progressed and eventually settled near the day’s lows on the monthly expiry day. The Nifty closed around 25,349, while the Sensex settled at 82,435.99, reflecting a broad-based deterioration in market sentiment," said Ajit Mishra, SVP – Research, Religare Broking.

"Sentiment remained subdued amid a sharp sell-off across global markets, particularly in US and Asian technology stocks, driven by concerns over AI-related valuations, the US interest-rate outlook and rising global risk aversion. Despite the correction, the broader domestic market backdrop continues to draw support from strong foreign investor inflows, which have exceeded USD 13 billion so far in November. Brent crude remained below USD92 per barrel, while the rupee opened stronger against the US dollar, providing some macroeconomic relief," Mishra added.

"The Nifty witnessed profit-booking after coming close to retesting the 26,000 mark and is likely to find support in the 25,000–25,300 zone. On the upside, the 25,650–25,800 zone is likely to act as an immediate resistance band. We recommend avoiding aggressive fresh exposure amid heightened volatility and using the possible consolidation to selectively accumulate quality stocks."

"From a sectoral perspective, banking and financials may take a breather following their sharp rally, while other rate-sensitive sectors such as auto and realty are likely to continue offering buying opportunities, alongside the pharma and healthcare basket," he added.

On Monday, the Indian rupee snapped its five-day winning streak and ended lower by 24 paise at 92.91 against the US dollar on Monday, compared with the previous session's close of 92.67.

"The rupee witnessed minor profit booking, declining around 30 paise to 92.90, as selling pressure emerged in the secondary equity market. Despite the correction, the broader currency trend remains supported by sustained foreign fund inflows, even with the Dollar Index near 103.80 and crude oil around $90," said Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities.

"Market participants will closely track FII activity this week, particularly after cumulative inflows of over ₹1 lakh crore, to assess whether foreign buying momentum continues into the final week of November. Going ahead, the rupee is expected to trade in a range of 92.50–93.55, with fund flows remaining a key driver," he added.
